title: hnscc-tls-signatures: analysis code and derived data for "Chemokine-based tertiary lymphoid structure signatures in head and neck cancer are redundant with generic inflammation and do not replicate prognostically"
description:
Reproducible analysis pipeline, derived patient-level data, and complete result tables and figures for the manuscript "Chemokine-based tertiary lymphoid structure signatures in head and neck cancer are redundant with generic inflammation and do not replicate prognostically" (submitted to Frontiers in Immunology, section Cancer Immunity and Immunotherapy).

Study summary. Chemokine-based transcriptional signatures are widely used as scalable surrogates for tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) in bulk tumour expression data. Using 438 patients from TCGA-HNSC and seven gene sets scored under three platform-agnostic algorithms, this study shows that (i) the three chemokine-based TLS signatures are nearly redundant with one another (Spearman rho >= 0.987); (ii) they correlate almost as strongly with a generic T cell-inflamed signature (rho = 0.89) as with each other; (iii) the consensus TLS score tracks checkpoint (rho = 0.898) and regulatory T cell (rho = 0.889) programmes far more strongly than the structural features of TLS, including germinal-centre B cells (rho = 0.462), plasma cells (rho = 0.496), and high endothelial venules (rho = 0.507); (iv) prognostically the score is cut-off dependent and not independent of stage and age (multivariable HR 0.757, 95% CI 0.463-1.238, p = 0.268), with discrimination (C-index 0.536) no better than a generic T cell-inflamed signature (0.546); and (v) HPV status does not confound the score's behaviour, although only 5 of 68 HPV-positive patients fall below the optimal cut-off, so a threshold-based chemokine score cannot discriminate within HPV-positive disease.

Contents. Twenty numbered pipeline scripts (cohort construction from the Genomic Data Commons, three-algorithm gene set scoring, consensus score construction, internal validation, microenvironmental programme correlation, nomogram and decision curve analysis, HPV status determination from in situ hybridisation / p16 immunohistochemistry / pathology-report text with a nested leave-one-out transcriptomic classifier, and HPV-stratified survival analysis); gene set definitions; derived patient-level analysis tables; all result tables and figures; and pipeline run logs. A second analysis layer adds the two independent external validation cohorts: a 270-patient surgical series (GSE65858, with HPV16 status resolved independently at both the DNA and the viral E6*I RNA level) and a 102-patient immunotherapy series (GSE159067); a 1,000-resample bootstrap assessment of cut-off stability, in which the whole selection procedure is repeated and, separately, the discovery cut-off is carried across unchanged; and a cross-platform validation in which the eight-gene transcriptomic HPV classifier is transplanted without re-fitting into GSE65858. The repository also carries the manuscript's supplementary material, including a 20-item REMARK reporting checklist mapped to the manuscript.

Licensing. Code is released under the MIT licence. Derived data and results are released under CC BY 4.0. Primary data are publicly available from the Genomic Data Commons under project TCGA-HNSC; no controlled-access or identifiable data were used.

Data handling note. Two GDC schema pitfalls that can silently corrupt a TCGA-HNSC cohort are handled explicitly: 172 of 528 participants carry more than one recorded diagnosis, so the analysis retains only the diagnosis flagged as primary disease with a squamous morphology code and a head-and-neck site of origin; and the deprecated field demographic.gender is replaced by demographic.sex_at_birth.

Retraction of an earlier claim. Release 1.0.0 of this repository stated that external validation was not possible because NCBI/GEO was unreachable from the analysis environment. That claim was wrong and is retracted: every request was being routed through an HTTP proxy that returns HTTP 000 for NCBI hosts. GEO is reachable over plain FTP, or over HTTPS to NCBI's IP with the proxy bypassed, which is how GSE159067 was retrieved and how the ArrayExpress mirror of GSE65858 was completed. Both external cohorts are now fully analysed. Remaining honest limitations: the prognostic claim does not replicate in either external cohort, the cut-off that generates the discovery-cohort survival difference is not reproducible under bootstrap resampling (only 37.6% of resamples select a threshold within 0.05 of the discovery value), and no cohort analysed here has paired tissue, so no transcriptomic surrogate could be validated against histologically quantified TLS.
